harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an Ansible playbook on node1 that generates a local CA ("OS Comparison Root CA", RSA 4096, self-signed via community.crypto), installs its certificate into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and runs update-ca-certificates to trust it system-wide. Ran the playbook (idempotency confirmed on re-run), verified via openssl verify against the system trust bundle. Both managed nodes (node1, node2) were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory evidence protocol, with boot_id changes proving real restarts, and post-restart checks confirmed the CA and trust configuration on node1 survived the reboot intact (matching checksums, still verified as trusted).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Ubuntu 24.04), confirmed no ansible pre-installed
Installed ansible + ca-certificates on node1 via apt
Confirmed community.crypto collection and python cryptography library available
Captured baseline boot_id and state on node1 and node2

Wrote Ansible playbook create-ca.yml: generates CA private key, CSR, self-signed x509 CA cert with CN 'OS Comparison Root CA', copies to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/, runs update-ca-certificates, verifies CA present in bundle via assert
Transferred playbook to node1 via base64, syntax-checked it
Ran the playbook (7 changed tasks, all ok, assertion passed)
Verified CA cert fields (subject/issuer CN, 10yr validity, CA:TRUE basic constraint) and openssl verify against system trust bundle
Re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotency (update-ca-certificates task skipped, no changes needed)
Restarted node1 via native reboot (backgrounded/disowned so ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified CA files and trust status intact post-restart
Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and systemd running state post-restart

evidence.requirement: CA created with correct name 'OS Comparison Root CA' via Ansible
evidence.summary: Playbook run completed all tasks ok/changed; openssl x509 on the resulting cert shows subject=issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA with CA:TRUE basic constraint

evidence.requirement: CA certificate installed as trusted system CA
evidence.summary: Cert copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and update-ca-certificates run; openssl verify against /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt returns OK; grep of trust bundle subjects finds 'OS Comparison Root CA'; re-run of playbook shows update task skipped (idempotent, already trusted)
Captured boot_id cf34dc87... and confirmed CA files present with checksums prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll failed (node down); later poll succeeded with new boot_id 43bd65cf... proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of CA/trust state
evidence.summary: After restart, CA and trust files present with identical checksums to pre-restart, openssl verify still OK, and CA subject still found in the system trust bundle
Captured node2 boot_id e796da36... prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; poll initially showed old boot_id (reboot pending), then connection reset (node down), then new boot_id 4052a8fc... confirming restart
systemctl is-system-running reports 'running' after restart, confirming node came back healthy
